:::{#thm-completeness}
#### Completeness of the real numbers

Let $A \subseteq \reals$ be nonempty.

- If $A$ is [bounded above](#def-bounded),
  the set of upper bounds of $A$ has a [minimum](#def-minimum).
- If $A$ is bounded below,
  the set of lower bounds of $A$ has a [maximum](#def-maximum).

:::

::: proof
The first statement is the least-upper-bound property of $\reals$
[@rudin1976principles, Definition 1.8, p. 4, and Theorem 1.19, p. 8].
For the second, let $-A = \cb{-a : a \in A}$.
Negating both sides of an inequality reverses it (@thm-neg-ineq),
so $\ell$ is a lower bound of $A$ exactly when $-\ell$ is an upper bound of $-A$.
The set $-A$ is nonempty and bounded above,
so by the first statement its upper bounds have a minimum $u$,
and then $-u$ is the largest lower bound of $A$.
:::
